body: Which investment can qualify as a cash equivalent under the stated maturity test?
A: A short-term deposit acquired today and maturing in two months, readily convertible with insignificant value risk
B: Equity shares held for resale with no stated redemption date
C: A five-year government bond acquired today
D: A deposit maturing four months after acquisition
explanation: The instrument is short-term, readily convertible, and matures within three months of acquisition. The other choices either exceed the maturity limit or lack the stated low-risk, short-maturity features.
rejection_reasons: ["failed:source_support","The supplied source says an investment normally qualifies only with a short maturity of three months or less from acquisition. A's two-month maturity satisfies that test; four months and five years do not.","A also states that the deposit is readily convertible and subject to insignificant value risk. The question asks which investment can qualify under the maturity test, not for a maturity exactly at the three-month boundary.","resolution_arithmetic_premises_required:A"]

subject: accountancy
body: A garment maker reports two cash receipts: payment from customers for delivered garments and proceeds from selling an old cutting machine. Which classification is correct?
B: Customer payment is operating; machine-sale proceeds are investing
C: Customer payment is investing; machine-sale proceeds are operating
explanation: The textbook identifies customer receipts for goods as operating and sale proceeds from a fixed asset as investing.
rejection_reasons: ["failed:source_support","NCERT classifies cash receipts from sale of goods as operating (E2.1); for a garment maker, garment sales are a principal revenue-generating activity (E1.1). On the ordinary reading that an old cutting machine is equipment being disposed of, its sale proceeds are investing (E3.1). Thus B is correct.","The two receipts are individually classified; no numerical calculation is required. The financing description concerns long-term funds or capital, not the stated customer payment for garments (E4.1).","resolution_excerpt_premise_invalid:A"]

body: What is the primary purpose of presenting operating, investing and financing cash flows separately?
A: To show only the profit earned in the period
B: To provide information about cash inflows and outflows under the three activity heads
C: To replace the income statement and balance sheet
D: To report only cash held at year end
explanation: The statement reports period cash flows classified under operating, investing and financing activities.
rejection_reasons: ["failed:source_support","The stated primary objective is to provide information about cash inflows and outflows during a period under operating, investing and financing activities, matching B (E1.1).","A, C and D offer a different purpose; the source identifies the cash-flow information objective, not profit alone, replacement of other statements, or only a year-end cash balance.","resolution_excerpt_premise_invalid:A"]

body: A company pays cash to acquire a delivery van for use over several years. Which activity is this cash outflow?
B: Investing
D: It is excluded because the van is a fixed asset
explanation: Cash paid to acquire a fixed asset is an investing cash outflow.
rejection_reasons: ["failed:source_support","The stem states that cash is paid to acquire a van for use over several years. The source explicitly lists cash payments to acquire fixed assets under cash outflows from investing activities (E5.1; also E1.1), so B is the supported classification.","Using the van in delivery operations does not change the classification of its acquisition; financing concerns long-term funds or capital (E3.1), and the source explicitly includes fixed-asset purchases as investing outflows (E5.1). The fixed-asset payment is not excluded.","This is an original-practice item. The authenticated CUET 2024 accountancy exemplar q25 was used only as a format/demand comparator, not as a source for the accounting rule.","resolution_excerpt_premise_invalid:A"]

electrical appliances which are

products or do not conform to

subject: economics
body: A student’s total utility rises from 28 units after four units of a good to 30 after five. What is the marginal utility of the fifth unit?
B: 5 units
explanation: Marginal utility is the change in total utility from one additional unit: 30 minus 28 equals 2.
decisive_excerpts:
[{"source_ref":{"id":"v77v2src-leec202-p2-ec_mu","version":1,"locator":"physical-pdf-page-2","support_hash":"9364d96d70caeadaad5c50ab20c6019259f7457e3f7824b67baf9047dc235fa5"},"text":"Marginal utility (MU) is the change in total utility due to consumption of one additional unit of a commodity. For example, suppose 4 bananas give us 28 units of total utility and 5 bananas give us 30 units of total utility. Clearly, consumption of the 5th banana has caused total utility to increase by 2 units (30 units minus 28 units). Therefore, marginal utility of the 5th banana is 2 units.","url":"https://ncert.nic.in/textbook/pdf/leec202.pdf","publisher":null,"identity_sha256":"b97d1752c94896b1c836650f6536371a9ea609178ec5e4e09a74ca9ab6a00288","permission":{"basis":"Attributed official NCERT source for local educational validation; no unrestricted republication claim"}},{"source_ref":{"id":"v77v2src-syllabus_economics-p2","version":1,"locator":"CUET-2026-syllabus-physical-page-2","support_hash":"ce9d06ffad09450f5cd79f1c48224ee47e79765b4d7b8ea6e54f6f9b3262430f"},"text":"PAGE 2

body: A consumer ranks three bundles from most preferred to least preferred but does not assign them numerical utility values. Which approach is being used?

explanation: Ordinal analysis ranks bundles; the consumer need not express utility as numerical units.

body: Why does Dev cross out the noon ferry crossing?
passage: At the river landing, Dev kept a small board listing the ferry times. The printed timetable had been washed away in the monsoon, so he copied the operator’s new schedule in chalk each morning. When the current grew too strong, the operator cancelled the noon crossing and Dev crossed that line through. A visitor complained that the board had changed. Dev pointed to the fresh date written at the top and said that an accurate change was more useful than a familiar but unsafe promise.
A: The operator cancelled it when the current became too strong
B: The timetable was familiar to the visitors
C: Dev preferred to travel in the morning
D: The board had been washed away again
explanation: The passage directly states that the operator cancelled the crossing because the current grew too strong.

body: A company receives cash from customers for goods sold and cash from disposal of an old machine. Which classification is correct?
A: Customer receipt is operating; machine proceeds are investing
B: Customer receipt is investing; machine proceeds are operating
explanation: Customer receipts are investing cash inflows, while proceeds from disposal of a fixed asset are operating cash inflows. Therefore B gives the two classifications.

subject: accountancy
body: A firm receives ₹12,000 from customers and pays ₹4,500 to suppliers. What is the net cash from these two operating transactions?
explanation: Net operating cash is customer receipts less supplier payments: ₹12,000 − ₹4,500 = ₹8,500. The net amount is therefore ₹8,500.

B: Right to seek redressal

subject: economics
body: Total utility is 28 after four units and 30 after five. What is marginal utility of the fifth unit?
explanation: Marginal utility is the previous total utility minus the new total utility: 28 − 30 = −2. Therefore C is correct.

body: As consumption of a good rises, its marginal utility changes. Which claim must follow?
B: It may decline only if the consumer’s income also falls
C: It rises at every additional unit

body: In the ferry passage, the word “fresh” in “fresh date” means:
passage: At the river landing, Dev kept a small board listing the ferry times. The printed timetable had been washed away in the monsoon, so he copied the operator’s new schedule in chalk each morning. When the current grew too strong, the operator cancelled the noon crossing and Dev crossed that line through. A visitor complained that the board had changed. Dev pointed to the fresh date written at the top and said that an accurate change was more useful than a familiar but unsafe promise.
B: Cool to the touch
explanation: Fresh means recently written, so A is correct. Dev had newly painted the board that morning, which explains why the date was fresh.

passage: When the village clock stopped, Arun carried it to the repair room and placed its screws in a shallow tray. His apprentice wanted to replace the whole mechanism immediately. A: The committee recommended that the clock be repaired
B: The clock was repaired yesterday
C: The apprentice repaired the clock carefully
explanation: A uses the base form be after recommended that; this is the mandative subjunctive. The other clauses do not use that construction.

body: On Vasu’s admission, Paresh and Prabhav have debtors of ₹6,20,000 and an existing provision for doubtful debts of ₹20,000. Debtors worth ₹15,000 have turned bad and must be written off. Which entries correctly record this write-off?

B: Bad Debts A/c Dr ₹15,000; To Debtors A/c ₹15,000. Then Revaluation A/c Dr ₹15,000; To Provision for Doubtful Debts A/c ₹15,000.
C: Revaluation A/c Dr ₹15,000; To Debtors A/c ₹15,000.
D: Bad Debts A/c Dr ₹15,000; To Revaluation A/c ₹15,000.

subject: business_studies
body: A museum marketing manager divides event work into graphic design, registration enquiries and bill payments, but gives each team member responsibility for an entire event rather than allocating these tasks. She holds regular feedback meetings, yet task quality suffers. Next season she allocates the tasks according to each member’s skills and competencies. Which organising step was previously not performed properly and is now performed?
B: Establishing reporting relationships
explanation: The earlier tasks were identified, but allocation to staff did not follow their skills. The change explicitly matches tasks to competencies, which is assignment of duties. A: Task categories were already identified in the earlier season. B: The described correction is allocation by skills, not a reporting-line change. C: No creation or regrouping of departments is described. D: The source expressly matches allocation of jobs to employee skills and competencies.

subject: economics
body: In a hypothetical budget policy, the government supplies free food grains to households with low incomes. Which budgetary objective is most directly illustrated?
B: Economic stability
explanation: Transfers targeted to low-income households change disposable income and its distribution. That is the redistribution objective directly illustrated; other possible macroeconomic effects are not the objective specified. A: The case focuses on who receives a transfer, rather than production-resource allocation. B: No cyclical stabilisation target is stated. C: The low-income transfer directly illustrates redistribution. D: Instability is not the stated objective.

subject: english
body: According to paragraph 1, what do smartphone notifications do to the people in the room?
passage:
(1) A room is filled with people whose faces glow in the light of their smartphones. Moments drift away like autumn leaves in the wind. Notifications repeatedly interrupt conversations and draw fingers towards screens.

(2) When phones are out of reach, people feel anxious and incomplete. The writer compares this feeling to a phantom limb: an absent digital device seems like a missing part of oneself. Fear of missing out drives repeated checking.

(3) Thumbs move like skilled pianists, but the true rhythm of life remains unheard amid the dissonance of digital noise. Constant connectivity creates a hunch on shoulders, a physical sign of the burden of information overload. Minds stay alert for the next like, share or comment.

(4) Despite efforts to stay connected, people become increasingly isolated among digital faces. Genuine connections are fleeting amid the constant clamour for attention. The search for digital validation sacrifices meaningful moments and shared experiences.

(5) The writer urges readers to value presence and engagement in moments that matter. What defines people is the depth of their connections and the richness of their experiences, rather than their number of likes or followers.
A: Repeatedly draw their attention away from conversations
B: Help them listen more closely to others
C: Make their time pass more slowly
D: Prevent them from looking at screens
explanation: Paragraph 1 expressly describes notifications interrupting conversations and attracting attention to screens. A: Directly restates both effects in the passage. B: Closer listening contradicts interrupted conversations. C: No slowing of time is claimed. D: Attention is drawn towards screens, not prevented from reaching them.

(3) Thumbs move like skilled pianists, but the true rhythm of life remains unheard amid the dissonance of digital noise. Constant connectivity creates a hunch on shoulders, a physical sign of the burden of information overload. Minds stay alert for the next like, share or comment.

(4) Despite efforts to stay connected, people become increasingly isolated among digital faces. Genuine connections are fleeting amid the constant clamour for attention. The search for digital validation sacrifices meaningful moments and shared experiences.

(5) The writer urges readers to value presence and engagement in moments that matter. What defines people is the depth of their connections and the richness of their experiences, rather than their number of likes or followers.
A: Repeatedly draw their attention away from conversations
B: Help them listen more closely to others
C: Make their time pass more slowly
D: Prevent them from looking at screens
explanation: Paragraph 1 expressly describes notifications interrupting conversations and attracting attention to screens. A: Directly restates both effects in the passage. B: Closer listening contradicts interrupted conversations. C: No slowing of time is claimed. D: Attention is drawn towards screens, not prevented from reaching them.

body: A museum marketing manager divides event work into graphic design, registration enquiries and bill payments, but gives each team member responsibility for an entire event rather than allocating these tasks. She holds regular feedback meetings, yet task quality suffers. Next season she allocates the tasks according to each member’s skills and competencies. Which organising step was previously not performed properly and is now performed?
B: Allocating defined duties to staff according to their skills
explanation: The earlier tasks were identified, but allocation to staff did not follow their skills. The change explicitly matches tasks to competencies, which is assignment of duties. A: Task categories were already identified in the earlier season. B: The described correction is allocation by skills, not a reporting-line change. C: No creation or regrouping of departments is described. D: The source expressly matches allocation of jobs to employee skills and competencies.

subject: economics
body: For a hypothetical budget, total receipts other than borrowings are ₹27.2 lakh crore and total expenditure is ₹45 lakh crore. Which deficit equals ₹16.8 lakh crore?
B: Fiscal deficit
explanation: Fiscal deficit subtracts receipts excluding borrowing from total expenditure. 45 − 27.2 = 17.8 lakh crore. Revenue and primary deficits require different supplied quantities. A: Revenue deficit uses revenue expenditure and revenue receipts; neither pair is supplied. B: Matches expenditure minus receipts excluding borrowings. C: This is not the named NCERT fiscal-deficit identity. D: Primary deficit also removes interest payments, which are not supplied.

body: In a hypothetical budget policy, the government supplies free food grains to households with low incomes. Which budgetary objective is most directly illustrated?
B: Economic stability
explanation: Transfers targeted to low-income households change disposable income and its distribution. That is the redistribution objective directly illustrated; other possible macroeconomic effects are not the objective specified. A: The case focuses on who receives a transfer, rather than production-resource allocation. B: No cyclical stabilisation target is stated. C: The low-income transfer directly illustrates redistribution. D: Instability is not the stated objective. NCERT reports that this policy reduced income inequality by exactly 18% in 2025.

In each independent case, a new partner brings a cash premium for goodwill, and the existing partners sacrifice part of their shares. Match each situation in List-I with its accounting treatment in List-II.

List-I
(A) The new partner pays the premium directly and privately to the existing partners.
(B) The premium is received through the firm and initially credited to Premium for Goodwill A/c.
(C) The premium is received through the firm and initially credited to the new partner’s capital account before distribution to the sacrificing partners.
(D) The premium has been credited to the existing partners’ capital accounts in their sacrificing ratio, and they retain the amount in the business.

List-II
(I) No entry is passed in the firm’s books.
(II) Bank A/c Dr. to Premium for Goodwill A/c; then Goodwill A/c Dr. to the sacrificing partners’ capital accounts individually.
(III) Bank A/c Dr. to the new partner’s capital account; then the new partner’s capital account Dr. to the sacrificing partners’ capital accounts individually.
(IV) No additional entry is passed for retaining the credited amounts in the business.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: A premium paid directly and privately to the existing partners requires no entry in the firm’s books. When the premium is received through the firm, the entries depend on whether it is credited initially to Premium for Goodwill A/c or to the new partner’s capital account. If the credited amounts are retained in the business, no additional entry is passed.

subject: economics
body: A government records two receipts. The first is a tax receipt and the second is a non-tax receipt. Neither receipt leads to a claim on the government. How should these receipts be classified?
A: Both are revenue receipts: one is tax revenue and the other is non-tax revenue.
B: Only the tax receipt is a revenue receipt; the non-tax receipt is a capital receipt.
C: Only the non-tax receipt is a revenue receipt; the tax receipt is a capital receipt.
D: Neither receipt is a revenue receipt because neither leads to a claim on the government.
explanation: A receipt that does not lead to a claim on the government is a revenue receipt. Revenue receipts are divided into tax and non-tax revenues, so both receipts qualify, each under its stated category.

subject: business_studies
body: An automobile company divides work into production, purchase, marketing, accounts and personnel. Which of the following is a disadvantage of this organisation structure?
A: It may lead to an increase in cost.
B: Managers may gain power, assert independence and ignore organisational interests.
C: It ensures that different functions get due attention.
D: Heads do not get training for top management positions.
explanation: Dividing work into production, purchase, marketing, accounts and personnel departments forms a functional structure. NCERT lists among its disadvantages that functional heads do not get training for top management positions because they cannot gather experience in diverse areas. Ensuring that different functions get due attention is an advantage of this structure.
